recipes.name: Awesome Sausage, Apple, and Cranberry Stuffing
ingredients_raw: 1 Golden Delicious apple, cored and chopped

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Spread white and whole wheat bread cubes in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until evenly toasted, 5 to 7 minutes. Transfer toasted bread cubes to a large bowl.

Cook sausage and onions in a large skillet over medium heat, stirring and breaking up lumps, until evenly browned, 6 to 8 minutes. Add celery, sage, rosemary, and thyme; cook and stir until flavors blend, about 2 minutes.
Pour sausage mixture over bread in bowl. Mix in chopped apple, dried cranberries, parsley, and liver. Drizzle with turkey stock and melted butter; mix lightly.
Allow stuffing to cool completely before loosely stuffing a turkey.

raw_recipe.headline: Awesome Sausage, Apple, and Cranberry Stuffing
raw_recipe.description: This apple sausage stuffing made with turkey sausage, herbs, apples, and dried cranberries is a tasty, fruity filling for your Thanksgiving turkey.

review.reviewBody: I've been making this recipe for a few years now, and since I started, it's demanded of me at every family get together. Like “Mommy of Four” I keep the dressing outside the turkey, and so compensate with extra broth. Make sure to spray your pan and keep it covered with foil! I’ve found that stirring it after it’s baked for 30 minutes or so, helps it bake more evenly. The only other changes I make are to throw in a little chardonnay for flavor and to add an egg for a little extra hold. I've also found that sage pork sausage is much more flavorful (make sure to drain it after cooking however). I have a habit of not measuring, so more cranberries and herbs always find their way in. And I cannot emphasize the difference FRESH herbs make. Experiment with different kinds of bread as well! Sourdough and potato bread have yielded delicious results. I've had a few flavor variations, but every result was just as tasty as the last. This is my favorite recipe from this site.

I love this recipe and have made it for a couple of years now. I use cubed day-old Italian Ciabatta bread and omit the giblets (I use the giblets to flavor my basting liquids for my gravy) and it is simply wonderful. I prepare this stuffing one day in advance w/o baking it (although fully cook the sausage, of course). Since I stuff my bird with other things (like onion, garlic, rosemary, lemon and orange), I make this the night before, very lightly grease a casserole dish, drizzle a very small amount of butter (just a bit) on the top to keep it moist and RESERVE ALL THE LIQUIDS UNTIL READY TO BAKE, pop it in the fridge overnight. The next day, add the liquids (broth and melted butter) - I usually add more broth since I will not be baking it in my turkey, it will need more broth (use your judgment depending on how much you are making), bring it to room temperature and then heat it through for about 35-45 minutes, ovens vary, so just make sure it is hot when ready to serve. It's a wonderfully delicious stuffing and the only one I will ever make. Thank you for sharing!

Excellent. Added one beaten egg to hold it together more. Doubled the stock (homemade) and doubled the butter. I'll chop the cranberries very small next time and reduce the amount. Used real herbs. Used pork sausage/less sodium. Baked 40 min w foil. Uncover and bake another 20.

This has become a family favorite! Just slightly altered to mix it up. I use 1/2 miltons wheat bread and half sourdough loaf, granny smith apple, sage sausage and all fresh herbs. I use chicken stock, no turkey livers and no parsley. I also do not cook it inside the turkey, but covered and cook at 350* for about 40 mins. Might need to add more chicken stock to get the right consistency. So so good and even better the next day!!

I make this stuffing each year and it is a staple at Thanksgiving. To save space in the oven I use a crock pot. Make the recipe as directed- I can fit a double batch in my large 6qt crock pot. I use a mix of white/wheat/cornbread cubed bagged stuffing mix, regular jimmy dean sausage, fresh herbs doubled what dry measurement is. I prep it all the day before and add it to the crock pot (minus butter & broth) I may measure some of the other stuff with my heart as well. On T-day I add broth, and butter- cover with a clean tea towel then the glass lid, and start it on low. The towel is key to it not getting soggy. I hope this helps someone else needing space in the oven!

I have been making this stuffing for years and it has become the one dish that everyone demands from me at Thanksgiving. We have renamed it "Five-Star Stuffing!" I use prepackaged Pepperidge Farms bread cubes (usually sage) and I skip the turkey liver. I make it a day or two before the feast and it makes the house smell amazing. Add a some broth or butter before/during cooking if it needs a little more moisture, and be sure to remove the foil at the end to crisp up the top.

HUGE HIT! I used pork sausage and doubled the recipe and it was fantastic. Like others, I cooked it outside the bird -- two 9×13 casserole dishes at 350 for 50 min covered with foil, then added more broth and cooked uncovered for 10. Omitted the liver. Used equal mix of white, wheat and sourdough. Added two eggs, but next time I'll add three. Used fresh thyme and rosemary (3/4 T each). Added salt, pepper and garlic powder. 

MY NEW GO-TO STUFFING!!

I’ve been making stuffing like this for years, and everyone loves it. I have tossed in a few fresh cranberries at times, with a little bit of whole berry canned cranberries (instead of dried)which means you might get a little tartness with sweetness in a bite here and there, but everyone really likes. I also usually make some for ‘in the bird stuffing’ and another ‘out of the bird stuffing’ casserole, since some love ‘in the bird stuffing’. (Definitely juicier). Definitely need more moisture if just baking in the oven, but still delicious! Only times I haven’t stuffed the bird is when my guys did a deep fried turkey, smoked the turkey, or as in the case this year trying rotisserie attachment for the Weber Kettle Grill over coals and letting that bird spin! So just finished making this great recipe to bake tomorrow!

Great recipe. My alterations:

-Used sourdough and cornbread
-Used sage turkey sausage 
-Used fresh herbs —measurements :
sage - 4 tsp rosemary -1.5 tbs thyme - 1 sprig

Used Chicken stock instead of turkey 
Used 3/4 cup extra of stock 
Used NO liver

Baked covered in foil 350F for 20 minutes, then turned off oven and left in for 1.5 hours.

BOMB.

The stuffing was a huge hit. I cooked it outside the bird. I made it with Gluten free bread. I bought a loaf of gluten free white and a loaf of gluten free ancient wheat to cut up and toast. I kept a close eye on them bcz over-toasting them isnt a great idea. I also used dried cranberries which added extra sweetness and a nice texture element. I tripled the recipe, used an entire box of turkey stock bcz it seemed REALLY dry without it. Our gluten intolerant guests were more than thrilled at Thanksgiving that they finally got to have stuffing again! I made enough for everyone and had 3 boxes of cardboard instant stuffing just in case it didnt turn out. One thing I wish I had done was to make this a day in advance. The flavors when combined overnight are so delicious and satisfying. TRY IT!
Absolutely delicious! I've made this for the last few years; I omit the liver and add bacon....so amazing my family and extended family love it!
I have been making this since 2001. Now my daughter makes it
I use a sage sausage (pork), no apples, chicken stock, and homemade sourdough. It comes out great, every time.

I thought the flavor of this dressing was wonderful, I made it in a 9 x 13 pan, using a bag of pepperidge farm seasoned stuffing. I doubled the broth but it was not enough, the bread croutons remained separated and did not hold together. I will definitely make it again but will add much more broth and perhaps an egg or two. The recipe as written is great as stuffing, needs some tweaking for dressing.
Like others I too added more broth to keep it from being too dry, but aside from that it’s extremely delicious….
This has been my go to stuffing recipe for at least 10 years. Delicious!!!!
This had become a Thanksgiving staple the last several years.
My family loves this stuff!! Thank you for posting
I make 4 boxes of jiffy cornbread and let it get stale overnight. I substitute this for the white bread. Everyone enjoys it.
